assessments.rationale: The HC reasoning on the omitted clause and post-scheme timing is textually strong for bondholders. The SC stay, leave granted, and RBI/Union backing, plus public-interest concern over bank resolution, favour the appellants. Adverse outcome is a meaningful minority risk with a large capital hit (~250 bps CET1) and likely dilution. Favourable outcome is partly priced in, so the upside is limited.

assessments.rationale: The HC reasoning on text and timing is strong, and the Bench's request for Cabinet records signals real doubt on process. Still, the SC stayed the order, the state and RBI defend the write-down, and courts are cautious about unwinding a 2020 rescue. Adverse outcome means a ~250 bps CET1 hit with dilution risk, and the market has priced little of it. Favourable outcome mostly removes an overhang.

Adverse outcome means ~250 bps CET1 hit and a likely raise, so the downside is larger than the upside, which is mostly relief already partly priced in.

Disclosure Under Regulation 30 Of The SEBI (Listing Obligations And Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 Disclosure under Regulation 3

verdict: Partly. The tracker would have flagged YESBANK from 26 Feb 2026 (judgment reserved; ₹8,415 cr = 13% of market cap) — 7.5 months before the drop — and put a legal-risk line on every technical signal. Claude Sonnet rated the ruling 40% likely to go against the bank at reservation and 40% at T-1, with an adverse move of -14%. The options market priced only ±5.3% to expiry, so long puts were cheap: the 21 PE bought at T-1 returned 6.0× by the verdict close. The catch is TIMING — the exact date is only knowable from the Supreme Court's next-day pronouncement list (captcha-gated; needs a manual check or a legal-news hit). Without it, rolling OTM puts from reservation returned 3.87× on premium paid. The post-verdict drift (short futures from the next open) worked without any foresight.
caveats: One event — this is a case study, not a backtest; base rates for SC outcomes are not established here.
The LLM may have absorbed post-as-of information in training; the prompt forbids it but can't guarantee it.
Settlement/close prices ignore bid-ask spread, STT and slippage; YESBANK options are liquid near ATM but far OTM fills are worse.
Lot size held at today's 31,100 for all legs.
The blind roll's March leg (19 PE → 1.77) paid off on an unrelated March sell-off, not the case; excluding it the roll still returned ~2.8× on premium.
